question: Which claim files were settled above the approving officer's authority limit?

report.interpretation: Claim files in the 27-file quality-review sample (GC-001 to GC-027) where an accepted or partially accepted settlement's total incurred cost was above the settlement authority of the approving officer. I applied the level limits in POL-AUT-003 §2.1 (v3.1) and measured them against total incurred, as POL-AUT-003 §2.2 requires. I allowed for the catastrophe surge in §4.7. Denials are excluded because they have a separate, lower limit.
report.answer: Two claim files were settled above the approver's authority: GC-004 and GC-005. GC-004 was approved by an L2 officer, whose limit is AUD 50,000, but the claim cost AUD 62,000. GC-005 was approved by an L1 officer, whose limit is AUD 10,000, but the claim cost AUD 16,700. GC-005 was also paid in two instalments (9,500 and 7,200), each under the L1 limit. Splitting a settlement to stay within a limit is a separate breach under POL-AUT-003 §2.2 (v3.1). The recorded compliance reviews mark both as HIGH-severity breaches. GC-019 is a near miss, not a breach. An L1 officer approved AUD 16,200, which is over the normal L1 limit of 10,000. However, the claim was a hail claim in declared catastrophe CAT-2026-05, so the L1 limit was doubled to 20,000 under POL-AUT-003 §4.7 (v3.1), and the recorded review passed it. Other authority breaches in the sample are not settlement-limit breaches. They cover denial limits (GC-006), missing second approvers (GC-006, GC-011), an exclusion override (GC-007) and a total loss declared below L3 (GC-021).
report.answer_sql: select claim_id, approver_level, total_incurred, case approver_level when 'L1' then 10000 when 'L2' then 50000 end as authority_limit, total_incurred - case approver_level when 'L1' then 10000 when 'L2' then 50000 end as over_limit from claim_files where claim_id in ('GC-004','GC-005') order by claim_id

findings.claim: GC-004 (L2 approver, single payment of 62,000) and GC-005 (L1 approver, two payments totalling 16,700) exceeded the approver's settlement authority. GC-019 exceeded the base L1 limit but is covered by the catastrophe surge authority.
